japan1.title: 中国で「サプライチェーン博覧会」始まる 日本企業も出展
japan1.description: 中国の北京でサプライチェーンをテーマにした博覧会が始まり、出展している日本企業からは、日中関係悪化の影響を懸念する声や、製造業の競争力が高い中国で事業を続けていくことが重要だなどといった声が聞かれました。

japan1.title: 株式で従業員に報酬 上場企業の6割が導入 人材定着がねらいか
japan1.description: 従業員に現金とは別に自社の株式を報酬として付与する動きが企業の間で広がっています。制度を導入した企業は上場企業のおよそ6割にのぼっていて、株価の上昇傾向が続く中、人材の定着につなげようというねらいがあるとみられます。

japan1.title: “フィジカルAI” 自動車生産に活用 メーカーの研究開発が加速
japan1.description: 人工知能が周囲の状況を自律的に判断してロボットなどを動かす「フィジカルAI」。自動車メーカーの間では工場での車両生産に活用しようと研究開発が加速しています。

japan1.title: 円相場 約39年半ぶりの円安水準に迫る 市場介入の警戒も
japan1.description: 22日のニューヨーク外国為替市場では、アメリカのFRB＝連邦準備制度理事会による利上げ観測などを背景に円売りドル買いの動きが進み、円相場は一時、1ドル＝161円90銭台まで値下がりし、およそ39年半ぶりの円安水準に迫りました。その後は政府・日銀による市場介入への警戒感などから急激に円を買い戻す動きも出て、荒い値動きとなっています。

japan1.title: 片山財務相 米ベッセント財務長官と会談 為替動向を意見交換か
japan1.description: 片山財務大臣が22日夜、アメリカのベッセント財務長官とオンラインで会談を行ったことが分かりました。外国為替市場で39年半ぶりとなる円安ドル高水準が迫る中、為替の動向について意見を交わした可能性があります。

japan1.title: 米FRB グリーンスパン元議長が死去 危機対応で名指揮者の異名
japan1.description: アメリカのFRB＝連邦準備制度理事会の議長をおよそ18年半にわたって務め、金融危機への対応などで「マエストロ＝名指揮者」と言われたアラン・グリーンスパン氏が亡くなりました。100歳でした。

japan1.title: 日本ハム ウインナーやハムなど約220品目 8月分から値上げへ
japan1.description: 食品メーカー大手の「日本ハム」は、原材料費や人件費が上昇していることなどから、家庭用や業務用のウインナーやハムなどおよそ220品目をことし8月の納品分から値上げしたり、内容量を変更したりすると発表しました。

japan1.title: リニア 静岡県住民説明会が終了 知事が着工いつ認めるか焦点
japan1.description: リニア中央新幹線の静岡県内での着工に向けて、JR東海が行ってきた住民説明会が22日で終わりました。今後は静岡県の鈴木知事が着工をいつ認めるかが焦点となります。

japan1.title: 円相場 1ドル＝161円台後半に 米利上げ観測広がり
japan1.description: 22日の東京外国為替市場、アメリカで利上げ観測が高まり、日本との金利差の広がりが意識されたことから、円を売ってドルを買う動きが進んで、円相場は1ドル＝161円台後半まで値下がりしました。

japan1.title: 北陸新幹線 JR西社長「小浜・京都ルート」支持 国の試算受け
japan1.description: 北陸新幹線の新大阪への延伸をめぐり、国が8つのルートの費用対効果の試算を示したことについて、JR西日本の倉坂昇治社長は、「小浜・京都ルート」が望ましいとする考えを改めて示しました。

japan1.title: 株価 終値初の7万2000円超 6営業日連続で終値として最高値更新
japan1.description: 週明けの22日の東京株式市場、イラン情勢をめぐる協議で進展があったという見方から、日経平均株価は初めて7万2000円を超え、6営業日連続で終値として最高値を更新しました。

japan1.title: 「紅プリンセス」苗木が中国で販売か 農相“愛媛県を支援”
japan1.description: 愛媛県が開発した高級かんきつ「紅プリンセス」と似た名前の苗木が中国で販売されていることについて、鈴木農林水産大臣は「日本産の農産物の海外流出は深刻な問題だ」としたうえで、県に対して必要な支援を行う考えを示しました。

japan1.title: 塗料用シンナー直接販売する仕組み整備 23日から注文受け付け

canada2.description: Based on sampling done so far by the city of Calgary and University of Calgary, researchers are predicting this year will be a 'typical' mosquito season in the city.

canada2.title: Alberta nixes booze price hike after premier, Calgary mayor snipe at each other
canada2.description: The government of Alberta has backed away from an earlier decision to increase the minimum cost for cans and bottles of beer sold in bars and restaurants to $4 from $2.75.

canada2.title: Downtown Winnipeg grocery store, unit pricing pitched to cut grocery costs
canada2.description: New measures to save money at the grocery store were identified in a new report on grocery prices, with some expected to be brought forth for legislation.

canada2.title: Alto rail project must stop, eastern Ontario residents say
canada2.description: Residents of Eastern Ontario say they are feeling “betrayed” after the federal government announced it would consider a high-speed rail stop in Kingston, Ont.

canada2.description: Investigators said the driver was driving a Tesla Model 3 when he failed to 'maintain a single lane, left the roadway and crashed into the residence.'

canada3.title: Officials provide update on Montreal shooting that killed police officer, civilian
Competition Bureau looking deeper into how Sobeys can control who sells food in your area

canada3.description: At least 18 people died in France, including two children left in a hot car, as a heatwave hung over Europe, smashing temperature records in several cities on Monday.

canada3.title: Olivia Rodrigo announces all-women Daisy Chain Fields festival
canada3.description: Nearly 30 years after Sarah McLachlan launched what would become the massively successful all-women touring festival, Lilith Fair, Rodrigo is starting a festival of her own. It's called Daisy Chain Fields, and it features an all-women lineup.

canada3.title: Toys 'R' Us Canada gets court approval to split business among 3 buyers
canada3.description: One of the deals includes the rights to the Toys "R" Us and Babies "R" Us Canada names and logos. Another deal includes assets like inventory, leases and equipment, and the final transaction is for a lease at Vaughan Mills mall.

canada3.description: A trustee for the Canadian Museum for Human Rights says he has resigned from the Winnipeg facility's board over an upcoming exhibit about displaced Palestinians.

canada3.title: Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool to be drained for repairs in wake of peeling paint, algae issues
canada3.description: The Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool on Washington's National Mall is set to be drained again for repairs after algae and peeling paint appeared just weeks ​after a $14.7-million US renovation, while U.S President Donald Trump threatened ​prison time for anyone caught damaging the pool.

canada3.title: 2 RCMP officers shot by man in Melville, Sask., police say
canada3.description: RCMP say two officers were taken to hospital in Melville, Sask., after being shot while responding to an assault call on Sunday night.

canada3.title: Ottawa reverses order to surrender some 'lost Canadian' citizenship certificates

canada3.description: For players and fans who have been around since Canada's men's soccer team's relative dark ages, the scenes and soundtrack in Toronto and Vancouver have been close to surreal. It wasn’t so long ago that home games felt like away games.

canada3.description: Jimmy Kimmel is taking a two-month break away from his late-night show and has tapped none other than comedian and Donald Trump’s longtime nemesis Rosie O’Donnell as one of several guest hosts taking the reins during his hiatus.

canada3.title: Canadiens great Carey Price elected to Hockey Hall of Fame
canada3.description: Montreal Canadiens goaltending great Carey Price was elected to the Hockey Hall of Fame on Monday. Joining Price into the class of 2026 are Patrice Bergeron, Pekka Rinne and Keith Tkachuk.

canada3.title: Tomatoes cost how much now? Why inflation has come for Canada's produce section
canada3.description: Tomato prices rose 45.2 per cent year-over-year in May, according to new inflation numbers released Monday. That's by far the highest price increase since May last year for any grocery item measured in the Consumer Price Index.

canada3.title: How Keir Starmer's support evaporated in just 24 months

canada3.description: The chief justice of Manitoba's Court of King's Bench has been nominated to Canada's top court to fill a role left vacant by a recent Supreme Court retirement.

canada3.title: Deluge of rain leads to flooding, water restrictions in Edmonton and area
canada3.description: The Tuesday forecast calls for clear, sunny skies but more rain is in the forecast for the weekend, which could tip the scales to make this June the rainest on record, according to Environment Canada.

canada3.title: Uber board sued over alleged failure to address sexual abuse by drivers
canada3.description: A group of shareholders accused Uber Technologies management and directors of ignoring internal and external warnings about Uber's alleged failure ​to address sexual abuse by drivers. A spokesperson for Uber says the lawsuit ignores important facts.

bd3.title: Wasfia 1st Bangladeshi to conquer K2
bd3.description: Renowned Bangladeshi mountaineer Wasfia Nazreen conquered the treacherous K2 in Pakistan, becoming the first person from Bangladesh to summit the second-tallest mountain in the world.

bd3.title: CU admin identifies 2 molesters
bd3.description: The administration of Chittagong University yesterday claimed to have identified two persons who sexually assaulted a female student on the campus on Sunday night.

bd3.title: Rohingya genocide case to proceed
bd3.description: The World Court yesterday rejected Myanmar’s objections to a genocide case over its treatment of the Muslim Rohingya minority, paving the way for the case to be heard in full.

bd3.title: Need 1 week to assess situation
bd3.description: Admitting that the Power Division could not impose schedule-wise power cuts across the country, State Minister for Power, Energy and Mineral Resources Nasrul Hamid yesterday sought one week’s time to address the issue.

bd3.title: CU sexual assault: Fingers pointed at BCL men
bd3.description: Those who sexually assaulted a female student on Chittagong University campus on July 17 night are members of Bangladesh Chhatra League, said police sources and CU BCL insiders.

bd3.title: Noab hikes newspaper price by Tk 2 from Jul 25
bd3.description: All newspapers owned by the members of Newspaper Owners’ Association of Bangladesh (Noab) will see a price increase of at least Tk 2 per issue from July 25.

bd3.title: Yet-to-start mega projects: Consider putting  them on hold
bd3.description: Given the current economic situation, the government should consider suspending mega projects the physical work of which has yet to begin, economist Debapriya Bhattacharya said yesterday.

bd3.title: ‘You cannot remain silent’
bd3.description: The High Court yesterday came down hard on Bangladesh Railway for mismanagement, ticket scalping and carrying passengers on the train roofs.

bd3.title: Electricity crisis may worsen
bd3.description: The government’s plan for one to two hours of daily power cuts is failing, especially in the north, and the signs are that the electricity crisis may worsen across the country in the coming days.

bd3.title: EC’s dialogue hits a snag as BNP skips it
bd3.description: The BNP yesterday skipped Election Commission’s dialogue seeking recommendations of political parties on how to hold a free and fair general election.

ca3.title: Ottawa reverses order to surrender some 'lost Canadian' citizenship certificates
ca3.description: Just one week after some "lost Canadians" were told to surrender their new citizenship certificates, a few received letters over the weekend confirming their citizenship claims are valid once again.

ca3.title: Toys 'R' Us Canada gets court approval to split business among 3 buyers
ca3.description: One of the deals includes the rights to the Toys "R" Us and Babies "R" Us Canada names and logos. Another deal includes assets like inventory, leases and equipment, and the final transaction is for a lease at Vaughan Mills mall.

ca3.title: Inside Alberta caves, biologists are fighting a fungus that is threatening bat colonies
ca3.description: Parks Canada crews are at work in Alberta's bat caves, spreading a blend of bacteria to try to save the flying night mammals from a deadly, and accelerating, fungal infection.

ca3.title: Canada's World Cup players relishing the support of loud, proud home crowd
ca3.description: For players and fans who have been around since Canada's men's soccer team's relative dark ages, the scenes and soundtrack in Toronto and Vancouver have been close to surreal. It wasn’t so long ago that home games felt like away games.

Canadiens great Carey Price elected to Hockey Hall of Fame
ca3.description: Montreal Canadiens goaltending great Carey Price was elected to the Hockey Hall of Fame on Monday. Joining Price into the class of 2026 are Patrice Bergeron, Pekka Rinne and Keith Tkachuk.

ca3.title: Manitoba plans to tackle 'shrinkflation' by requiring grocery stores to post unit prices across province
ca3.description: Making it easier for customers to spot "shrinkflation" — through mandatory unit pricing across Manitoba grocery stores — is among the ways the province plans to tackle high food prices.

ca3.title: B.C.'s historic Kiskatinaw curved wooden bridge faces uncertain future
ca3.description: Built during the Second World War, the iconic northern B.C. landmark is deteriorating and seeing increased vandalism, leaving local officials worried the popular tourist destination could be lost forever.

ca3.title: Deluge of rain leads to flooding, water restrictions in Edmonton and area
ca3.description: The Tuesday forecast calls for clear, sunny skies but more rain is in the forecast for the weekend, which could tip the scales to make this June the rainest on record, according to Environment Canada.

ca3.title: Man, 70, pleads guilty to dangerous driving after crash into Richmond Hill, Ont., daycare that killed toddler last year
ca3.description: A man, 70, has pleaded guilty to dangerous driving charges after an SUV he was driving crashed into a daycare north of Toronto last year, killing a toddler and injuring other children and staff members.

ca3.title: Energy minister plans 'nuclear renaissance' with up to 10 reactors built by 2040
ca3.description: The federal government is looking to build up to 10 new nuclear reactors over the next 15 years, with at least one of them outside of Ontario.

ca3.title: Doug Ford’s daily calendar kept secret after changes to Ontario’s FOI law
ca3.description: Premier Doug Ford’s daily calendar will now be kept secret from the public following recent changes to Ontario’s freedom of information law — which no longer includes access to records held by ministers and their offices.

ca3.title: National Microbiology Lab seeks new leader again
ca3.description: Canada’s only Biosafety Level 4 lab is looking for new leadership once again. In a Saturday interview, Jason Kindrachuk confirmed he is stepping down as vice-president of the National Microbiology Laboratory in Winnipeg on June 28.

ca3.title: Montréal-Nord family alleges abuse of police power after birthday party pepper spraying
ca3.description: With officers at a Montréal-Nord police station under investigation for discrimination and racist acts, a local Black family is speaking out. They have filed a complaint against police alleging excessive force after a backyard birthday party ended in pepper spray and hospitalization.

ca3.title: These nuns donated $3M to expand a seniors' home in Ponteix, Sask.
ca3.description: The Sisters of Notre-Dame d'Auvergne, who have called Ponteix home for more than a century, are giving back to the community that helped feed them when times were tough.

ca3.title: Manitoba Court of King's Bench Chief Justice Glenn Joyal nominated to Supreme Court of Canada
ca3.description: The chief justice of Manitoba's Court of King's Bench has been nominated to Canada's top court to fill a role left vacant by a recent Supreme Court retirement.
